values.name: __finding_id__
values.description: Identifier of the originating CSPM / posture finding supplied by the detection layer. The ingest adapter fetches __posture_finding__ by it.

values.name: __posture_finding__
values.description: The posture finding the adapter fetched for __finding_id__, exactly finding_id, rule_ref (the baseline rule that fired), resource_ref, baseline_ref (the baseline version evaluated), misconfiguration_class (public_exposure, over_permissive_identity, network_exposure, missing_encryption or baseline_deviation), upstream_severity (informational, low, medium, high or critical), source (cspm_scan or iac_guardrail), first_observed_at (Zulu) and changed_at (the control-plane change that introduced the deviation, or null when unknown).

values.name: __ingested_at__
values.description: Zulu instant (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) the finding is ingested at.

values.name: __posture_case__
values.description: Envelope the ingest step emits: the normalised finding, its fingerprint (SHA-256 of rule and resource), and detection_latency_minutes when the introducing change is known.

values.name: __inventory_record__
values.description: The cloud-inventory record for the affected resource, exactly resource_ref, container_ref (the account, subscription, project or tenant), region, resource_type and classification; null, or empty from n8n, when the inventory has none, which the enrichment records as an inventory gap.

values.name: __ownership_record__
values.description: The ownership-graph record for the resource, exactly owner_ref and active (a real boolean); null, or empty from n8n, when the graph has none.

values.name: __default_owner_ref__
values.description: The operator's declared default ownership pool, which receives the case when the ownership graph has no active owner for the resource.

values.name: __severity_policy__
values.description: The operator's classification policy: each classification label mapped to a whole-number shift from -2 to +2 bands applied to the upstream severity.

values.name: __exception_ledger__
values.description: Exception-ledger entries, each exactly exception_ref, kind (time_boxed_exception, compensating_control or known_deviation), rule_ref, resource_ref, owner_ref, valid_from (Zulu), expires_at (Zulu, or null when open-ended) and attestation_ref (or null). CACAO v2 has no list type, so the value rides as a string carrying a JSON-native list; the compile target's adapter seam marshals it.

values.name: __prior_closures__
values.description: Earlier closed cases from the case ledger, each exactly case_ref, rule_ref, container_ref, outcome (verified, suppressed or escalated) and closed_at (Zulu). CACAO v2 has no list type, so the value rides as a string carrying a JSON-native list; the compile target's adapter seam marshals it.

values.name: __resolved_at__
values.description: Zulu instant (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) the resource context is resolved at.

values.name: __resource_context__
values.description: Envelope the enrichment step emits: the resource and its container, the owner with any fallback, the upstream and resolved severity with the shift and its basis, known_false_positive as a real boolean with the matched and the rejected ledger entries, and the recurrence verdict.

values.name: __resource_id__
values.description: Cloud resource identifier (URN, ARN or path-style resource id) the finding is bound to. Extracted at the compile target's adapter seam from __resource_context__.resource_id.

values.name: __owner_id__
values.description: Identity (team or individual) accountable for the resource, or the default pool when the ownership graph has no active owner. Extracted at the compile target's adapter seam from __resource_context__.owner_id.

values.name: __severity__
values.description: Resolved severity of the finding (informational, low, medium, high or critical), which selects the notification channel. Extracted at the compile target's adapter seam from __resource_context__.severity.

values.name: __known_false_positive__
values.description: Whether a live, exact, time-boxed exception-ledger entry covers the finding; true routes to suppress-and-close, false to owner notification. Extracted at the compile target's adapter seam from __resource_context__.known_false_positive. A real boolean: the gate compares it to true, and the string 'false' is truthy in most runtimes.

values.name: __closed_at__
values.description: Zulu instant (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) the suppressed case is closed at.

values.name: __suppression_closure__
values.description: Envelope the suppression step emits: the closure linked to the matched ledger entry and its expiry, with no remediation attempted and nobody paged.

values.name: __severity_routing__
values.description: The operator's pre-bound channel for each resolved severity: exactly informational, low, medium, high and critical, each the reference of a ticketing, chat or paging channel.

values.name: __runbook_ref__
values.description: The guided-remediation runbook for the violated baseline rule, carried on the owner notification.

values.name: __notified_at__
values.description: Zulu instant (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) the owner is notified at.

values.name: __owner_notification__
values.description: Envelope the notification step emits: the owner and whether it is the default pool, the channel bound to the resolved severity, the finding, the resource, the violated baseline and the runbook.

values.name: __remediation_attempt__
values.description: The remediation attempt from the operator's change surface, exactly mode (iac_change, runbook_execution or manual_change), change_ref (the change record), approved_by (the operator's approver, required for an automated hand-off, or null), actor_ref and applied_at (Zulu).

values.name: __remediation_recorded_at__
values.description: Zulu instant (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) the remediation attempt is recorded at.

values.name: __remediation_record__
values.description: Envelope the guided-remediation step emits: the attested change (mode, change record, approver, actor and applied_at) and the NIST SP 800-53 anchors of its branch.

values.name: __rescan_result__
values.description: The targeted re-scan result, exactly rule_ref, resource_ref, baseline_ref, result (pass, fail or not_evaluated) and evaluated_at (Zulu).

values.name: __verified_at__
values.description: Zulu instant (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) the re-scan verdict is given at.

values.name: __rescan_verdict__
values.description: Envelope the re-scan step emits: the re-scan result, remediation_verified as a real boolean, the first failing reason when it is false, and the remediation latency when it is true.

values.name: __remediation_verified__
values.description: Whether the re-scan verified the remediation; true closes the case, false escalates. Extracted at the compile target's adapter seam from __rescan_verdict__.remediation_verified. A real boolean: the gate compares it to true.

values.name: __paging_channel_ref__
values.description: The security-engineering on-call's pre-bound paging channel.

values.name: __escalated_at__
values.description: Zulu instant (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) the escalation is raised at.

values.name: __escalation__
values.description: Envelope the escalation step emits: the finding, the attempted remediation, the failing re-scan evidence with its reason, and the recurrence verdict, for the security-engineering on-call.

nodes.name: ingest finding
nodes.notes: Normalise the CSPM / posture finding the adapter fetched for __finding_id__ (__posture_finding__) into the case every later step reads. The finding may come from a continuous CSPM scan or from an IaC policy guardrail emitting the same shape at deploy time; the case fingerprint is the baseline rule and the resource, so both report the same deviation identically. Detection latency, and the MTTD stamp, are set only when the adapter names the control-plane change that introduced the deviation. Produces __posture_case__.

nodes.name: enrich resource and owner

parameters.pythonCode:
from content.playbooks.cloud_misconfiguration.primitives.context import resolve_resource_context
__resource_context__ = resolve_resource_context(case=__posture_case__, inventory=__inventory_record__, ownership=__ownership_record__, default_owner_ref=__default_owner_ref__, severity_policy=__severity_policy__, exceptions=__exception_ledger__, prior_closures=__prior_closures__, resolved_at=__resolved_at__)

nodes.notes: Resolve the affected resource against the cloud inventory and the ownership graph. The owner is the graph's active owner, or the operator's default pool when there is none, with the fallback recorded. Severity is the upstream severity shifted by the operator's classification policy, never lowered for a resource the inventory does not know. The finding is a known false positive only when a live exception-ledger entry names this rule and this resource, carries an expiry and, for a compensating control, is attested; lapsed matches are listed with the reason. Recurrence is read from the prior closures as the recurring-misconfiguration KRI defines it. Produces __resource_context__, from which __resource_id__, __owner_id__, __severity__ and __known_false_positive__ are extracted.

nodes.name: known false positive?
nodes.notes: Suppression branch on __known_false_positive__, extracted from __resource_context__. on_true: a live, exact, time-boxed exception-ledger entry covers the finding; suppress and close. on_false: continue into owner notification.

nodes.name: suppress and close
nodes.notes: Close the case on the ledger entry the enrichment matched, without a remediation attempt and without paging, and account the closure against the recurring-misconfiguration KRI so a chronically suppressed posture rule surfaces in the metrics layer. The step never extends or widens the entry, and refuses to close once the entry has lapsed. Produces __suppression_closure__.

nodes.name: notify owner

parameters.pythonCode:
from content.playbooks.cloud_misconfiguration.primitives.notification import compose_owner_notification
__owner_notification__ = compose_owner_notification(case=__posture_case__, context=__resource_context__, routing=__severity_routing__, runbook_ref=__runbook_ref__, notified_at=__notified_at__)

nodes.notes: Notify the resource owner on the operator's pre-bound channel for the resolved severity; the routing binds one channel for each of the five severities. The notification carries the finding, the affected resource, the violated baseline and the guided-remediation runbook, and says so when the owner is the default pool. Produces __owner_notification__.

nodes.name: guided remediation

parameters.pythonCode:
from content.playbooks.cloud_misconfiguration.primitives.remediation import record_remediation_attempt
__remediation_record__ = record_remediation_attempt(case=__posture_case__, notification=__owner_notification__, attempt=__remediation_attempt__, recorded_at=__remediation_recorded_at__)

nodes.notes: Record the remediation attempt against the finding with change-management attestation. The change itself is operator-bound: an IaC change or runbook execution handed off with the operator's approver, or an owner-driven manual change. Every attempt cites its change record, and a change applied before the finding was first observed cannot be its remediation. Produces __remediation_record__, carrying the NIST SP 800-53 anchors of the branch.

nodes.name: re-scan

parameters.pythonCode:
from content.playbooks.cloud_misconfiguration.primitives.verification import verify_remediation
__rescan_verdict__ = verify_remediation(case=__posture_case__, remediation=__remediation_record__, rescan=__rescan_result__, verified_at=__verified_at__)

nodes.notes: Read the targeted re-scan of the same baseline rule against the same resource; the re-scan is a deterministic verification, not a fresh posture sweep. The remediation is verified only by a pass, under the same baseline version, evaluated after the change; otherwise the verdict carries the first failing reason. Produces __rescan_verdict__, from which __remediation_verified__ is extracted.

nodes.name: remediation verified?
nodes.notes: Branch on __remediation_verified__, extracted from __rescan_verdict__. on_true: the rule no longer fires; close the case. on_false: the remediation did not stick, so escalate rather than close on an unverified attempt.

nodes.name: escalate

parameters.pythonCode:
from content.playbooks.cloud_misconfiguration.primitives.escalation import compose_escalation
__escalation__ = compose_escalation(case=__posture_case__, context=__resource_context__, remediation=__remediation_record__, verification=__rescan_verdict__, paging_channel_ref=__paging_channel_ref__, escalated_at=__escalated_at__)

nodes.notes: Escalate to the security-engineering on-call on the operator's pre-bound paging channel. The payload carries the finding, the attempted remediation and the failing re-scan evidence with its reason, and repeats the recurrence verdict; the escalation is tracked against the recurring-misconfiguration KRI. Produces __escalation__.

parameters.content:
## Cloud misconfiguration remediation
`playbook.cloud_misconfiguration@v1` · content v1.0.0 · maturity: stable · compiled from a CACAO 2.0 playbook by SecOps-NG

Respond to a cloud-posture (CSPM) finding that flags a sensitive misconfiguration: public storage exposure, over-permissive identity, missing encryption, or a deviating baseline. The playbook enriches the finding with resource ownership, notifies the responsible owner via the operator's pre-bound channel, guides the remediation through an attested change, and re-scans to verify the fix. Failed re-scans escalate so a recurring misconfiguration cannot quietly persist. CACAO v2…

**Regulatory anchors**
- NIS2 Directive (EU) 2022/2555, Article 21(2)(e) — security in network and information systems acquisition, development and maintenance, including vulnerability handling and disclosure
- NIS2 Directive (EU) 2022/2555, Article 21(2)(i) — human-resources security, access-control and asset-management policies
- DORA Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, Article 9 — ICT risk-management framework (protection and prevention)
- DORA Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, Article 19 — reporting of major ICT-related incidents (escalation path when a posture exception becomes incident-grade)

**Controls:** 3 control reference(s) in the canonical source, mapped under `content/mappings/`.

**Before you run it**
- Inputs the trigger expects from you: `__finding_id__`, `__posture_finding__`, `__ingested_at__`, `__inventory_record__`, `__ownership_record__`, `__default_owner_ref__`, `__severity_policy__`, `__exception_ledger__`, `__prior_closures__`, `__resolved_at__`, `__closed_at__`, `__severity_routing__`, `__runbook_ref__`, `__notified_at__`, `__remediation_attempt__`, `__remediation_recorded_at__`, `__rescan_result__`, `__verified_at__`, `__paging_channel_ref__`, `__escalated_at__`
- Code nodes name the deterministic primitive each step runs; bind them to where your primitives execute, or replace the body:
  - ingest finding → `content.playbooks.cloud_misconfiguration.primitives.finding.normalise_posture_finding`
  - enrich resource and owner → `content.playbooks.cloud_misconfiguration.primitives.context.resolve_resource_context`
  - suppress and close → `content.playbooks.cloud_misconfiguration.primitives.suppression.compose_suppression_closure`
  - notify owner → `content.playbooks.cloud_misconfiguration.primitives.notification.compose_owner_notification`
  - guided remediation → `content.playbooks.cloud_misconfiguration.primitives.remediation.record_remediation_attempt`
  - re-scan → `content.playbooks.cloud_misconfiguration.primitives.verification.verify_remediation`
  - escalate → `content.playbooks.cloud_misconfiguration.primitives.escalation.compose_escalation`
- This file carries no credentials; connectors and secrets are yours to attach.

**Source** https://github.com/secops-ng/secops-ng-framework/tree/main/content/playbooks/cloud_misconfiguration
